title: architecture-standards-api-coding-model-serving-observability-performance-adr-2026-03-25
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This page consolidates Redwood Inference's canonical architecture and standards across API design, coding conventions, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, and performance. It is intended as the single source of truth for engineering teams implementing production-facing services and model endpoints. The guidance below is normative; exceptions require an ADR and approval from the Platform Architecture guild.

Scope
- Public and internal HTTP/GRPC APIs (inference-gateway, console-api, billing-service)
- Model serving components (redwood-runtime, model-router, kv-cache-service)
- Infra patterns for cloud-hosted, dedicated, and private deployments
- Observability (metrics, traces, logs, SLOs) and performance expectations

Key Principles
- Backwards-compatibility first: non-breaking defaults and schema evolution strategy (see ADR section).
- Clear ownership: every service must declare an owner_team and SLA in the service registry.
- Predictable performance: tiered SLOs for hosted vs dedicated customers.
- Observable by default: instrumentation, dashboards, and trace context propagation required.

1) API Standards
- Protocols: Prefer REST+JSON for public SDK/backwards compatibility and gRPC for internal high-throughput services (model-router <-> redwood-runtime).
- Versioning: Use semantic API versions in the URL (/v1/, /v2/) and stable Accept/Content-Type versioning header: Accept: application/json;v=2026-03. Deprecation policy: 90-day minimum notice for breaking version removals for hosted customers.
- Contract: Request/response schemas must be defined in OpenAPI v3 for REST endpoints and Protobuf for gRPC. Schema repo: git.redwood/internal-schema.
- Error handling: 4XX for client errors, 5XX for server errors. Use structured error envelope: {"code","message","request_id","details"}.
- Rate limiting: Token bucket per-customer at gateway with default quotas: 1000 rps per customer (hosted), burst=2000 for 30s. Dedicated customers may configure per-contract.

API Example (REST generation request):
```json
POST /v1/generate
Content-Type: application/json;v=2026-03
{
  "model": "redwood-rm3-small",
  "input": "Summarize the following text...",
  "max_tokens": 256
}
```

2) Coding Standards
- Languages: Go for core runtime components (redwood-runtime, model-router), Python for SDKs and evals, TypeScript for web/console frontends.
- Go conventions: Follow Effective Go and the internal linter config (golangci-lint ruleset at infra/linters/go.yml).
- PR requirements: All changes must include unit tests, integration tests for public API changes, and a changelog entry if behavior changes. Code owners must approve via CODEOWNERS.
- Secrets & keys: Never commit secrets. Use vault.redwood.company for KMS/HSM-managed secrets. CI gates will fail builds if secrets detected.

3) Infra Standards
- IaC: Terraform modules in infra/modules (versioned semantically). Environments: dev, staging, prod. All changes to prod require an RFC + automated canary deployment job.
- Networking: Services use private subnets, egress via NAT gateways, and internal service-to-service communication uses mTLS via our service-mesh (linkerd). Public ingress goes through inference-gateway and edge WAF.
- Capacity: GPU fleet managed by gpu-fleet-controller. Dedicated pools are in separate accounts/projects per-customer. Autoscaling config: CPU/queue-length based for control-plane services; GPU pool scaling uses queued inference backlogs + utilization thresholds (scale-up when avg util > 70% for 2m).

Configuration table (examples):
| Component | Default SLO (p50/p95/p99) | Scale trigger | Owner |
| inference-gateway | 40ms / 120ms / 350ms | >80% CPU 1m | eng-infra |
| redwood-runtime (lm inference) | 10ms/token / 40ms/token / 120ms/token | queued requests > 100 | eng-serving-runtime |
| metrics-ingest | 1s / 3s / 10s | backlog > 5000 | eng-platform |

4) Model-serving Standards
- Model packaging: All models submitted to model-onboarding must include: model-card.md, quantization profile, compatibility matrix (supported sequence lengths, kv-cache handling), and a test prompt set.
- Serving runtime: redwood-runtime must support: continuous batching, KV cache sharing, prompt prefix caching, and quantization variants. Kernel selection is automated via runtime compilation heuristics.
- Rollouts: Canary 5% -> 20% -> 100% over 24-72 hours with automated quality checks (latency, token cost, eval suite pass rate). Use rollout tool: deployments/rollout-cli.
- Fallbacks: model-router must be configured with fallback variants (e.g., rm3-small-quant -> rm3-small-fp16) and region failover policies.

5) Observability Standards
- Traces: W3C TraceContext required. High-cardinality attributes prohibited on spans unless approved.
- Metrics: Use Prometheus naming conventions; every service should export: request_count, request_duration_seconds (histogram), error_count, queue_length. SLI definitions are in eng-sre/sli-definitions.md.
- Logging: Structured JSON logs with keys timestamp, level, service, request_id, trace_id, message. Sensitive fields must be redacted before emission.
- Dashboards and Alerts: Standard dashboards per service; alert thresholds defined in eng-platform/alerts. On-call playbook must be linked from service runbook.

6) Performance Standards
- Latency & Cost: For hosted API, target p95 token latency <= 120ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens) and cost-per-1k-tokens optimized via batching and KV cache. Quantization must not degrade accuracy beyond 1% absolute on regression prompt set.
- Benchmarks: All model and runtime changes require a perf-suite run (eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite) with comparison against baseline. Benchmarks capture tail latency, throughput, and memory usage.

7) ADR: API Schema Evolution and Model Versioning (ADR-2026-03)
Title: Semantic schema versioning + content-negotiation for forward-compatible APIs
Status: Accepted
Decision date: 2026-03-04
Rationale:
- We operate multiple deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private) and frequently onboard new model variants. Breaking API changes cause high customer support and integration costs. A single approach to versioning reduces operational burden.
Decision:
- Enforce semantic schema change rules: additive changes are backwards-compatible; breaking changes require a new major API version and an ADR.
- Implement content negotiation header versioning (Accept/Content-Type;v=YYYY-MM) in addition to URL versioning. This allows gradual rollout and per-client pinning.
- Model-serving contracts (model-card + model-schema.json) are stored alongside OpenAPI/proto defs. Model releases must include a compatibility matrix and an automated contract test.
Consequences:
- Integration tests will exercise both the default and the previous major version for a 30-day overlap window. SDKs will expose explicit version flags.
- Infra: API gateways will route based on Accept header for canary flows.
Rollout plan:
1. Update OpenAPI generator to emit versioned Content-Type by 2026-04-15.
2. Add Accept header routing to inference-gateway by 2026-04-30 (canary 10% traffic).
3. Update public SDKs to default to latest stable version but allow version pinning.
4. Publish deprecation policy and migration guides in product-docs.
Owner: Platform Architecture Guild (owner_team: engineering).

Appendix: Quick checklists
- New service onboarding checklist: owner declared, OpenAPI/proto in schema repo, metrics & traces instrumented, runbook + alerting, perf baseline recorded.
- Model onboarding checklist: model-card, quant profile, test prompts, compatibility matrix, baseline evals, rollout policy.
